D.summary: Bitcoin is $82,583, 1.43x off its July 1 low of $57,748, boxed between the $79,736 October low (a daily close under it breaks the bounce) and the $87,364 September high (a weekly close above it is the green light). Your $95k-by-year-end call has history on its side but not the options market: 5 of 6 past-cycle analogs touched $95k by Dec 31 and all 6 did by Feb 19, while IBIT options price only about a 23% chance BTC finishes above $95k on Feb 19. $95,420 is also the 1.272 fib extension of the Jul-Sep run, so it's a real chart target. "4x off the bottom" from this cycle's low is $230,992, a cycle-top number, not a this-year number; 4x the 2022 low was $62,396, and that already happened. Own mostly BTC right now: dominance just hit a 14-month high (60.14% on CoinGecko) and ETH/BTC is down 9.3% in 30 days, so alts only get the money after dominance closes back under 57%. The only coins on our watch list beating BTC are TIA, NEAR, INJ, SAND; INJ is 3.9% from its takeoff trigger. Best option for the $95k idea: the IBIT Feb 19 2027 $47/$55 call spread at $280 a spread. Breakeven is about $88,050 BTC, it pays 2.41x at $95k and tops out at 2.86x ($520 profit) from about $97.2k up. Max loss $280.

macro_summary: Money came out of tech last week and went into oil and Treasuries. The Nasdaq (QQQ) fell 5.5%, long bonds (TLT) rose 2.7%, VIX jumped to 19.99, oil (WTI) sits at $101.41 on Hormuz risk, and the 10-year yield is 5.1%. Fed net liquidity (balance sheet minus Treasury cash minus reverse repo) is $5.872T, down $114.6B in 13 weeks because the Treasury's cash pile grew $127.2B. That is a headwind, not a tailwind. Junk-bond spreads widened 0.53 points in a month to 3.23%, a warning light but not a crisis. Inverse gravity right now: when BTC drops, the dollar (90-day correlation -0.36), oil (-0.44 over 30 days) and yields tend to rise. Gold has been moving WITH BTC (+0.51), so it isn't a hedge for it right now. Crypto's own fuel is mixed: stablecoins are $304.6B, up $1.1B in 30 days but below the $315.5B May 17 peak, while spot BTC ETFs bled $228.4M over the last 5 trading days.
